embeds.title: 🔴 New HTTP/2 Bomb DoS Attack Crashes Web Servers in Under a Minute
embeds.description:
Researchers at offensive security firm Calif discovered a new denial-of-service attack called HTTP/2 Bomb that combines HPACK compression amplification with HTTP/2 flow-control stalling to exhaust server memory. The technique affects default configurations of NGINX, Apache HTTP Server, Microsoft IIS, Envoy, and Cloudflare Pingora. A single client on a 100 Mbps connection can exhaust tens of gigabytes of RAM within seconds, with Envoy and Apache httpd exhausting 32 GB in approximately 10-18 seconds respectively. Patches have been released for nginx (version 1.29.8) and Apache httpd mod_http2 (version 2.0.41, CVE-2026-49975), but no patches are available for IIS, Envoy, or Pingora at the time of writing.
**Sources:** BleepingComputer, CSO Online • 🟡 2 corroborating

embeds.title: 🟢 Cisco Patches CVE-2026-20230 in Unified Communications Manager
embeds.description:
Cisco has patched CVE-2026-20230, a server-side request forgery vulnerability in Unified Communications Manager that allows an unauthenticated attacker on the network to write arbitrary files and escalate to root privilege. Cisco's PSIRT reports it has not yet seen the flaw exploited in attacks, though proof-of-concept exploit code is publicly available. The vulnerability only affects deployments with the WebDialer service enabled, which ships off by default.
